title: Ligand Nano-cluster Arrays in a Supported Lipid Bilayer
protocol: Arrange glass cover-slides on a multi-slide tray made of Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE).
Immerse the tray with slides and the observation chamber in a surfactant solution suitable for cleaning quartz cuvettes.
Ultra-sonicate in the surfactant solution for 30 min at room temperature between 20 and 30 °C.
Rinse 5 times with ultrapure water (18.2 M.cm, 0.059 µS/cm).
Ultra-sonicate in surfactant solution for another 30 min at room temperature between 20 and 30 °C.
Rinse the slides 10 times with ultrapure water.
Repeat steps involving ultra-sonication and rinsing twice more.
Store in water at room temperature between 20 and 30 °C for up to one week.
Deposit a suspension of silica beads (2% v/v, 70 µL) drop by drop on a cover-slide held at an inclination of 15 degrees.
Let the suspension spread for about 1 min while flipping the glass by 90° every 15 s.
Allow the liquid to evaporate under ambient conditions.
Store in a clean glass or PTFE chamber at ambient conditions for up to 2 days.
Place the prepared slides inside a radio frequency (RF) magnetron sputtering equipment on a rotating table at a distance of about 105 mm from an aluminum (99%) : silicon (1%) target.
Pump down the deposition chamber to 2.6 x 10^-4 Pa using a turbo-molecular pump.
Introduce pure Argon atmosphere (5N, 99.999%) with a flux of 10 s.c.c.m. at a pressure of 0.8 Pa.
Switch on the RF power generator.
Sputter for 2 min keeping the shutter closed to remove possible impurities from the surface of the target.
Open the shutter and allow the sputtering to continue for 60 min to deposit aluminum on the glass slide to a thickness of 200 nm.
Cut the flow of argon, close the gate valve to isolate the turbomolecular pump from the deposition chamber.
Vent the chamber with clean nitrogen to obtain the room pressure.
Recover the aluminum-coated slides.
Store for up to a month in a clean and hermetically sealed glass or PTFE box under ambient conditions.
Immerse the aluminum-coated slide in ultrapure water.
Ultra-sonicate the immersed slide for 30 seconds in an ultrasonic bath.
Deposit 0.5 mL of (3-aminopropyl)-triethoxysilane at the bottom of a desiccator.
Place the glass slides on a ceramic grid and inside the desiccator.
Connect the desiccator to a membrane pump and run at maximum power for 30 minutes.
Close the valve of the desiccator and switch off the pump.
Heat the desiccator to about 50 °C for 1 hour.
Open the desiccator and collect the slides.
Transfer the collected slides to another clean desiccator for storage up to 48 hours at room temperature.
Place one slide on a PTFE support.
Deposit 1 mL of 25 µg/mL BSA-biotin dissolved in PBS.
Leave the slide with BSA-biotin solution for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Rinse the slide 10 times with PBS.
Store the sample for up to 24 hours at 4 °C away from light source.
Incubate the slides in a solution of NaOH in PBS overnight at room temperature.
Remove the water in the PTFE enclosure of the Langmuir trough using a pump.
Clean the PTFE enclosure with a lint-free non-woven disposable towel soaked in chloroform.
Clean the PTFE enclosure four times with lukewarm ultrapure water (40 to 50 °C).
Clean the PTFE enclosure at least six times with cold ultrapure water.
Place PTFE trays in the PTFE enclosure of the Langmuir trough and then fill it with ultrapure water.
Set the measured pressure to 0 mN/m using the control software of the Langmuir apparatus.
Deposit 30 µL of a 1 mg/mL lipid solution (DOPC in chloroform) on the surface of the water using a gastight glass/metal syringe.
Use the control software to compress the lipid monolayer by closing the PTFE barrier until the desired pressure (27 mN/m for DOPC) is reached.
Use the control software to dip the glass slide into the PTFE enclosure using a motorized clamp.
Hold the slide, in the clamp, perpendicular to the air-water interface.
Raise the slide slowly at 15 mm/min through the interface while maintaining a constant pressure of 27 mN/m.
Place the slide in a dry environment for immediate use or store it up to 24 hours at room temperature between 20 and 30 °C.
Maintain the surface pressure in the Langmuir trough at 27 mN/m using the control software of the Langmuir apparatus.
Add a small amount of lipid, if necessary, to achieve the desired pressure of 27 mN/m.
Place glass slides carrying the lipid monolayer horizontally on the water's surface.
Ensure each slide is floating above a PTFE tray without tilting it.
Push one slide at a time into its corresponding PTFE tray using PTFE or metal tweezers, ensuring they are immersed in the water.
Transfer PTFE trays containing slides into a crystallizer filled with ultrapure water using PTFE or metal tweezers.
Ensure that the slides are not exposed to air during transfer.
Use PTFE or metal tweezers to transfer a bilayer coated glass slide into an observation chamber underwater.
Ensure that about 1 mL of water is trapped inside the chamber after closing it while working under water.
Take the assembled chamber out of the water and check for leaks, ensuring it remains water-tight.
Replace the 1 mL of ultrapure water in the observation chamber with PBS by adding and removing 500 µL of PBS ten times.
Introduce 100 µg/mL of bovine serum albumin (BSA) into the observation chamber containing the prepared slide.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature (between 20 and 30 °C).
Rinse the bilayer by removing and adding 500 µL of PBS ten times.
Add fluorescent or non-fluorescent neutravidin (NAV) at 2 µg/mL into the chamber containing the prepared slide.
Incubate for 30 minutes at room temperature (between 20 and 30 °C).
Rinse by adding and removing 500 µL of PBS 10 times.
Add biotinylated anti-CD3 at 2 µg/mL to the chamber containing the slide.
Leave for 30 min at room temperature (between 20 and 30 °C).
Rinse by adding and removing 500 µL of PBS 10 times.
Replace the PBS with cell medium (PBS + 0.1% BSA) by adding and removing 500 µL of the cell medium 10 times.
Leave 200 µL of cell medium in the chamber with the slide.
Place the chamber for 10 min at 37 °C before adding cells.
Deposit 400 µL of the cell suspension into the chamber carefully.
Incubate the cells for 30 min at 37 °C.
Fix the cells with 2% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 15 min at 37 °C.
Replace the PFA with PBS by repeated removal and addition of 500 µL of PBS.
Use a fluorescence microscope to image the protein pattern in epi-fluorescence mode using appropriate illumination wavelength (639 nm) and filter cubes.
